function: Excluded, no_learning: BS beamforming and RIS phase shifts are solved by SCA-ADMM optimization (p. 5-7); the FL CNN is the application the link serves (p. 9), aggregated digitally (p. 3).
notes: Title page 1 matches the DOI (FL-assisted RIS active and passive beamforming with ADMM). p. 6: the beamforming subproblem is a quadratic program for which "the optimal solution can be obtained using the ADMM algorithm", with closed-form updates (Eqs. 44-47, 61-64) and no trained parameters; p. 8 Algorithm 1 iterates alpha, beta, theta, Phi until a threshold, and p. 8 gives complexity O(N^3 K^3 + L^3) for this classical algorithm. The only learned model is a CNN for "real-time equipment fault prediction" trained with FL (p. 2, p. 9), so learning is the application that the link serves, not a physical-layer function. p. 3: the BS aggregates the received updates with channel-norm weights (Eqs. 3-4), a digital weighted average and not over-the-air computation, so the federated-learning exception of no_learning does not apply and the problem is not area 7. Baselines (p. 9-11) are SCA, P-BF, RCG, random phase shift, FedAvg, all non-learned or the FL itself. If a reviewer counts the FL model as the learned element, the next code would be function, because digital aggregation is outside area 7; the decision is exclude either way. Channel is a custom Ricean simulator (p. 8-9).
